configuration: The official MUDPACK test driver code/mudpack/test/tmud24.f, unmodified except for one output block appended before the program's final `end` that writes the solved real grid array `phi(nx,ny)` (one value per line, the real value per grid point, fixed column-major order with the first listed dimension fastest) and the driver's own final discretization-error scalar, to `sab_solution.dat`. No solver call, problem coefficient, boundary condition or grid size is changed from the official test.
observable: the solved real grid field phi and the driver's own printed discretization error, both pointwise
runtime_note: under 300 s: the whole check (library build, driver compile and link, and the fixed-size single multigrid solve) measured well under one second natively
variant: ic/variant/driver.f differs from ic/nominal/driver.f only in the literal value of `xb`, changed from 1 to 1.0000000000000004: exactly two upward binary64 ULPs (the build uses -fdefault-real-8, so Fortran REAL is 8-byte). This is an active input to the PDE problem set-up (a domain-extent bound the driver uses to place the grid and evaluate boundary/coefficient/exact-solution values), so the perturbation propagates into the right-hand side, the boundary conditions and the solved field.
altbuild: declared: run.sh altbuild builds the same pinned source (code/mudpack/src and this check's unmodified driver.f) with gfortran -O0 instead of -O2, same -fdefault-real-8 -std=legacy; MUDPACK's default build is already IEEE (no fast-math to flip), so -O0 is the same-compiler fallback axis. selfcheck grades it against nominal and records the distance as this check's floor.

evidence.floor_how: measured by selfcheck on 2026-09-16: run.sh altbuild (the same pinned source (driver.f and code/mudpack/src) built with gfortran -O0 instead of -O2, same -fdefault-real-8 -std=legacy; MUDPACK's default build is already IEEE (no fast-math to flip), so -O0 is the same-compiler fallback axis) against run.sh nominal, graded with the check's own validate.py: all graded values within bound

altbuild.what: the same pinned source (driver.f and code/mudpack/src) built with gfortran -O0 instead of -O2, same -fdefault-real-8 -std=legacy; MUDPACK's default build is already IEEE (no fast-math to flip), so -O0 is the same-compiler fallback axis

warrant: code/mudpack/test/tmud24.f sets tolmax=0.0 (no iterative error-control flag): the multigrid solve runs a fixed cycle count (maxcy), so the discretization error the driver itself prints (errmax=0.337E-05 at this grid resolution, matching output/darwin.dp) is the scale a wrong algorithm (a dropped coefficient term, a coarser grid, fewer cycles, a broken relaxation sweep) would violate. Provisional atol=1e-10, rtol=1e-09 sit many orders of magnitude below that discretization scale while leaving headroom above binary64 round-off (about 1e-15 relative); selfcheck's variant (two-ULP input) and altbuild (-O0) floors are the measured evidence and this paragraph is revised with their numbers before the final selfcheck.
